defects.source_says: Executive Order 12107 (signed 1978-12-28, 44 FR 1055) section 2-404: 'Except as otherwise specifically provided in this Order, this Order shall be effective on January 1, 1979.' The amendment could not take effect in 1976, before the order was signed. The claim's own judgment_reason for each of these clauses and its research_rationale give 1979-01-01, so the claim is internally inconsistent.

defects.claim_says: Section 1 (conversion of Treasury Department Schedule B employees in protective-function positions) continues operative; no later event other than the EO 12107 name substitution
defects.source_says: The claim does not address the transfer of the protective function (the Secret Service) out of the Treasury Department to the Department of Homeland Security in 2003, although its own cited lead, 5 CFR 9701.604(d)(15), is a DHS regulation applying the order to DHS employees. Whether the order's 'employee of the Treasury Department' predicate still has a subject, or reaches DHS employees by a statutory transfer or reference provision, is a later event bearing on the current predicate that the claim leaves unanalysed.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11203.txt (sha256 0af81452... matches; all 31 quoted spans match the bytes; identical to jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11203.txt)
jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12107.txt (sha256 e734f497... matches; sections 2-101(b) list includes 11203; 2-404 effective date 1979-01-01; 2-202 savings applies to revoked orders)
jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s3301.txt (note prints order as amended by EO 12107, no ending)
cruden number search EO:11203 (7 hits in 5 files; no revocation or supersession) and bare-number grep of held FR order texts
packet dossier EO:11203 (13 clause scopes; inventory matches)
reasoning: Identity (EO 11203, signed 1965-03-12, 30 FR 3417, FR Doc. 65-2731) agrees with the held Federal Register text, the census register and the OFR catalog. All quoted spans match the hashed text, and the 13-clause inventory matches the order and the packet. No own-terms end, revocation or supersession was found in the held texts or the OFR catalog; the only disposition note (amended by EO 12107) is addressed, and the substitution of the Office of Personnel Management for the Commission in sections 1(3), 1(4) and 5 is correctly treated as an amendment. The claim is rejected because the later_events on those three clauses give the amendment an effective date of 1976-01-01, which contradicts EO 12107 section 2-404 (effective 1979-01-01), predates the amending order's signature, and contradicts the claim's own judgment reasons and rationale. The current predicate also omits any analysis of the 2003 transfer of the Secret Service from Treasury to the Department of Homeland Security, which bears on whether the Treasury-specific conversion authority still operates as written. The operative outcome may well be right, since the DHS regulation at 5 CFR 9701.604 and the 2024 OPM Schedule B listing still invoke the order, but the claim has to state that basis.

defects.claim_says: Its text has no savings clause and no held later text names it.
defects.source_says: The claim's own research_rationale and earlier_end_check state that the held 1989 OFR codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_12235.txt) names and prints the order, and that the held U.S. Code text (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t15-s3364.txt) prints it in the 15 U.S.C. 3364 note. 'No held later text names it' is false as written and contradicts the rationale. The accurate statement, which the cruden search supports, is that no held later executive order or other later instrument names it.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12235.txt (sha256 4ca8957e... matches; all 10 quoted spans match the bytes)
jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t15-s3364.txt (3364(d) delegation authority current; note prints order with '[now Administrator]' bracket and no ending)
jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv (release point 119-121 has 15 U.S.C. 717z and 3361 'Delegation of Functions' notes citing the order, which shows those sections are still printed)
cruden number search EO:12235 (3 hits, all in the 1989 codification) and bare-number grep of held FR order texts, including EO 13286 (no hit)
packet dossier EO:12235 (4 clause scopes; inventory matches)
reasoning: Identity (EO 12235, signed 1980-09-03, 45 FR 58803, FR Doc. 80-27464) agrees with the held text, the census register and the OFR catalog. All quoted spans match the hashed text. The four-scope inventory covers 1-101, 1-102, 1-103, 1-104 and 1-105, and the claim discloses that the text-layer scope sec1-102-a joins the tail of 1-102 with 1-103 and 1-104. The preamble is an authority recital. No own-terms end, amendment, revocation or supersession was found: the OFR catalog has no note, the cruden search finds only the 1989 codification, and EO 13286 does not name the order. The current predicate for 1-101 and 1-104 rests on the held current text of 15 U.S.C. 3364(d). For 1-102, the claim correctly says it does not hold 15 U.S.C. 717z; the current-law mentions show that 717z and 3361 are still printed with delegation notes in release point 119-121, which supports the operative outcome. The FEMA title change is handled correctly as an editorial bracket. The claim is rejected on one point: the savings reason says no held later text names the order, which contradicts the rationale's own account of the 1989 codification and the U.S. Code note. The statement needs to be limited to later instruments. The outcome (yes, all clauses operative) otherwise appears sound.
